item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors surged +$12.1 billion i...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors surged +$12.1 billion in September, to a record $86.9 billion.
This marks the 2nd-largest monthly increase in history, following the record +$14.7 billion increase in July 2026.
Since the start of 2024, imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors have more than quadrupled.
YoY, these imports rose +151%, the largest YoY increase on record, compared with peak annual growth of just +34% during the 2000 Dot-Com Boom.
Based on September's figures, these imports are now running at an annualized rate above $1.0 trillion for the first time.
US demand for technology hardware is exploding.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global crude oil in transit is up to 1.28 billion barrels, an all-time high. This figure...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global crude oil in transit is up to 1.28 billion barrels, an all-time high.
This figure has surged +180 million barrels over the last several weeks.
This comes as Middle Eastern oil flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes, while more crude remains at sea for longer.
Ship-to-ship transfers are keeping oil aboard tankers for longer, while extended shipping routes are increasing transit times.
Meanwhile, global oil importers diversifying away from the Middle East are lengthening voyages, leaving more crude tied up aboard tankers.
As a result, more oil remains in transit rather than being readily available to refiners, tightening near-term supply despite recovering export flows.
Oil is flowing, but timely delivery is becoming the bottleneck.

item.title: @Hedgeye: 🇺🇸 Americans are borrowing to keep up: Consumer credit jumped $27.8 billion in September, the mos...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
🇺🇸 Americans are borrowing to keep up:
Consumer credit jumped $27.8 billion in September, the most since November 2022 and more than double the roughly $12 billion expected.
In the same month, real disposable income fell 0.3% and the personal saving rate slid to 3.8%, the lowest since October 2022.
This comes as inflation takes a bigger bite out of every paycheck.
With the PCE price index up 0.5% in a single month and CPI up 3.7% from a year ago, households leaned on credit just to keep real spending flat.
Credit card demand rose the most in four years in the Fed’s latest loan officer survey, and banks pointed to higher prices as the main reason.
That debt isn’t cheap. The average rate on cards charging interest is 22.36%, the highest in a year, and the Fed just raised rates for the first time since 2023.
The last time borrowing ran this hot and saving ran this thin was late 2022.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US job openings jumped +333,000 in September, to 7.52 million, the 3rd-highest reading si...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US job openings jumped +333,000 in September, to 7.52 million, the 3rd-highest reading since November 2024.
This marks the largest monthly increase since April and the 3rd-largestsince October 2024.
The surge was led by professional and business services, which added +106,000 openings.
State and local government, excluding education, followed, with an increase of +104,000.
As a result, the ratio of job openings to unemployed workers rose to 1.06, its highest since January 2025.
There are now 414,000 more available vacancies than unemployed workers, the 2nd-largest difference since January 2025.
US labor demand appears to be recovering.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Retail demand for stocks is incredibly strong: Retail investors purchased US equities in the 22 con...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Retail demand for stocks is incredibly strong:
Retail investors purchased US equities in the 22 consecutive sessions ending November 3rd, the 3rd-longest streak since the memestock mania in 2021.
This also ranks as their 6th-longest purchasing streak since 2017.
Over this period, retail investors bought ~$33 billion in equities, their 5th-largest purchase since 2017.
This equals an average of ~$1.5 billion per trading session, and +40% above the trailing 12-month average.
Year-to-date, retail investors have purchased a record +$251 billion in equities, surpassing the previous full-year record of +$241 billion set in 2021 and marking a +134% increase from the same period last year.
Retail continues to buy the dip.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$MSFT WINDS DOWN AI CLOUD DEAL WITH $ORCL
Microsoft has reportedly declined to renew its 2023 agreement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle and has been gradually shutting down that capacity in recent months, Bloomberg reports.
The deal was originally intended to power an AI-enhanced version of Bing.
However, the Oracle servers used older-generation Nvidia GPUs that no longer met Microsoft's computing specifications.
Oracle says demand for its AI infrastructure remains strong, including for older-generation GPUs.
item.content:encoded:
$MSFT WINDS DOWN AI CLOUD DEAL WITH $ORCL

Microsoft has reportedly declined to renew its 2023 agreement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle and has been gradually shutting down that capacity in recent months, Bloomberg reports.

The deal was originally intended to power an AI-enhanced version of Bing.

However, the Oracle servers used older-generation Nvidia GPUs that no longer met Microsoft's computing specifications.

Oracle says demand for its AI infrastructure remains strong, including for older-generation GPUs.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investors took record leverage into this week's decline:
US leveraged ETFs attracted +$9.5 billion in inflows in the week ending October 16th, their largest weekly intake on record in data going back to 2006.
This is more than double the previous weekly record inflow of +$4.5 billion, set in 2024.
By comparison, the largest weekly outflow was -$7.5 billion in late 2025.
This comes as the 3x leveraged long Semiconductor ETF, SOXL, attracted +$7.0 billion in inflows that week, its largest weekly inflow on record.
At the same time, the 3x leveraged long Nasdaq 100 ETF, TQQQ, attracted +$1.3 billion.
Investors are highly levered amid the volatility.

item.title: @Hedgeye: The best part about risk managing Bear Markets? They bounce. The crowd sells the low end of the ran...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
The best part about risk managing Bear Markets? They bounce.
The crowd sells the low end of the range inside a Bearish TRADE and TREND. Then it buys the bounce toward the top end.
Backwards.
The process does the opposite. Cover some of your shorts near the LRR. Re-load into the bounce toward the TRR.
Same tape. Opposite playbook.

item.title: @wallstengine: TSMC WEIGHS MAKING 3D DRAM AT NVIDIA'S REQUEST $TSM has reportedly begun drawing up plans to manufa...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TSMC WEIGHS MAKING 3D DRAM AT NVIDIA'S REQUEST
$TSM has reportedly begun drawing up plans to manufacture advanced 3D DRAM chips as AI-driven memory shortages push chip designers to seek additional supply, per The Information.
Unlike conventional DRAM, 3D DRAM stacks memory cells vertically to increase density.
The move could put TSMC in direct competition with Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.
No production timeline has been set. TSMC is considering building new fabs or converting an existing facility, but says its focus remains on its core logic foundry business.

item.title: @wallstengine: $ASTS TO BUILD ITS OWN REUSABLE ROCKET AST SpaceMobile announced plans to develop Blacklift, a 20-t...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$ASTS TO BUILD ITS OWN REUSABLE ROCKET
AST SpaceMobile announced plans to develop Blacklift, a 20-ton reusable rocket designed to carry up to five BlueBird satellites per launch, with operations targeted for late 2028.
The company has signed a $1.3B+ agreement with Firefly Aerospace $FLY, which includes:
- Engines for the first three Blacklift rockets. - A perpetual license for AST to manufacture Firefly's Miranda and Vira engines at a new U.S. facility. - Engineering support over three years.
AST will pay approximately $800M upfront, consisting of $400M in cash and 10M–14M $ASTS shares, plus $250M for engines and $250M for engineering support.
Importantly, AST will continue using external launch providers, with existing agreements covering more than 100 BlueBird satellites for deployment in 2027–2028.
AST plans to unveil Blacklift on November 12 in New York City.

AST SpaceMobile announced plans to develop Blacklift, a 20-ton reusable rocket designed to carry up to five BlueBird satellites per launch, with operations targeted for late 2028.

The company has signed a $1.3B+ agreement with Firefly Aerospace $FLY, which includes:

- Engines for the first three Blacklift rockets.
- A perpetual license for AST to manufacture Firefly's Miranda and Vira engines at a new U.S. facility.
- Engineering support over three years.

AST will pay approximately $800M upfront, consisting of $400M in cash and 10M–14M $ASTS shares, plus $250M for engines and $250M for engineering support.

Importantly, AST will continue using external launch providers, with existing agreements covering more than 100 BlueBird satellites for deployment in 2027–2028.

AST plans to unveil Blacklift on November 12 in New York City.

item.title: @wallstengine: FIREFLY SIGNS $1.3B+ ROCKET ENGINE DEAL WITH $ASTS $FLY has signed a 3-year agreement with AST Spac...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
FIREFLY SIGNS $1.3B+ ROCKET ENGINE DEAL WITH $ASTS
$FLY has signed a 3-year agreement with AST SpaceMobile to supply engines for AST's new heavy-lift rocket.
Under the deal:
Firefly will deliver 36 engines, including 27 Miranda and 9 Vira engines, for AST's first three rockets.
AST will receive a license to manufacture the engines, along with engineering support. Firefly retains ownership of the engine IP.
AST will pay Firefly more than $1.3B in a combination of cash and ASTS shares, with the shares subject to lock-up periods.
For AST, the goal is to gain greater control over its launch schedule. For Firefly, the additional funding will help expand engine testing capacity and accelerate production of its own launch vehicles.
item.content:encoded:
FIREFLY SIGNS $1.3B+ ROCKET ENGINE DEAL WITH $ASTS

$FLY has signed a 3-year agreement with AST SpaceMobile to supply engines for AST's new heavy-lift rocket.

Under the deal:

Firefly will deliver 36 engines, including 27 Miranda and 9 Vira engines, for AST's first three rockets.

AST will receive a license to manufacture the engines, along with engineering support. Firefly retains ownership of the engine IP.

AST will pay Firefly more than $1.3B in a combination of cash and ASTS shares, with the shares subject to lock-up periods.

For AST, the goal is to gain greater control over its launch schedule. For Firefly, the additional funding will help expand engine testing capacity and accelerate production of its own launch vehicles.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US diesel inventories dropped -3.6 million barrels last week, to 99.3 million barrels, th...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US diesel inventories dropped -3.6 million barrels last week, to 99.3 million barrels, the lowest level since May 2003.
Since January 2026, distillate fuel oil inventories have declined -33.7 million barrels, or -25%.
Furthermore, the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -399,000 barrels last week, to 282.2 million barrels, its lowest since October 1982.
Since March, oil inventories in the SPR have dropped by -133.2 million barrels, or -32%.
Meanwhile, commercial crude oil stocks excluding the SPR declined -865,000 barrels last week, to 409.8 million barrels, their lowest reading since July 31st.
US fuel reserves are being depleted at a rapid pace.

item.title: @wallstengine: The future of robotics might involve a lot less real-world training. Think about it. Training physi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
The future of robotics might involve a lot less real-world training.
Think about it. Training physical robots through trial and error is expensive, slow and difficult to scale.
Moonlake just demonstrated it.
Starting with only 50 real-world demos, they ran reinforcement learning across 384 simulated environments, all at once.
And the improvements actually carried over to the physical robot. In one sorting test, it went from correctly sorting 6 out of 45 parts to 23. https://x.com/moonlake/status/2118405991662493737/video/1

item.title: @wallstengine: The IRS has increased the income thresholds for its 2027 tax brackets, as shown in the chart. Here'...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
The IRS has increased the income thresholds for its 2027 tax brackets, as shown in the chart.
Here's how much less you'd owe in federal income tax if your income stays the same as in 2026.
Single filers: $50K salary: $68 less $100K salary: $281 less $250K: $923 less
Married filing jointly: $100K combined income: $136 less $200K combined income: $561 less $500K combined income: $1,846 less
All seven tax rates remain unchanged. The savings come from wider income brackets and higher standard deductions.
Calculations assume the standard deduction, with no additional deductions or tax credits.
item.content:encoded:
The IRS has increased the income thresholds for its 2027 tax brackets, as shown in the chart.

Here's how much less you'd owe in federal income tax if your income stays the same as in 2026.

Single filers:
$50K salary: $68 less
$100K salary: $281 less
$250K: $923 less

Married filing jointly:
$100K combined income: $136 less
$200K combined income: $561 less
$500K combined income: $1,846 less

All seven tax rates remain unchanged. The savings come from wider income brackets and higher standard deductions.

Calculations assume the standard deduction, with no additional deductions or tax credits.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Anthropic has now disclosed a record $895 billion in future AI infrastructure spending commitments....
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Anthropic has now disclosed a record $895 billion in future AI infrastructure spending commitments.
This includes both purchase commitments and leases for computing power and related infrastructure.
$448 billion, or 50%, is expected to be incurred by the end of 2030, with ~$70 billion due over the next 12 months.
The biggest commitments are to Broadcom, $AVGO, at $161 billion, followed by Google at $121 billion, with up to $150 billion in additional estimated spending on Google's AI chips.
Anthropic has also committed up to $121 billion to SpaceX, $SPCX, and at least $110 billion to Amazon, $AMZN.
For perspective, among Big Tech companies, only Alphabet, $GOOGL, has larger commitments, at $1.06 trillion, while Meta, $META, follows with $866 billion.
The scale of Anthropic's spending obligations is unprecedented.

item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
🩸 BLOOD IN THE STREETS
The Nasdaq 100 is down -5.3%, more than 13% below its Oct. 6 record high.
The S&P 500 is down -3.3%, on pace for its worst day since April 2025.
Chips are leading the way down.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is off -9.5%, Nvidia -8% and AMD -16%.
Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough added $QQQ to the short side in ETF Pro Plus yesterday.
Our $DRAM short, added Oct. 21, is down -15.2% since.
On the long side, Keith is in health care, consumer staples, utilities and Treasuries.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: On today's stock market crash: As an investor, on days like today, you have to ask yourself one que...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
On today's stock market crash:
As an investor, on days like today, you have to ask yourself one question: What fundamentally changed over the last 24 hours?
The shift in the fundamental backdrop cannot be attributed solely to the Midterm Election results; markets had already largely priced in the outcome.
So, what changed between yesterday and today? What is the fundamental reason for today's decline?
One of the most likely catalysts is growing concern about a potential "ban" on AI, or at the very least, severe regulation of the industry.
Over the last 24 hours, Democratic lawmakers have publicly called for restrictions on advanced AI development, including an outright "ban on artificial superintelligence."
Frankly, an outright ban will not happen.
Such a ban, if even possible to enforce, would effectively mean the US surrendering its position in the global AI race to China.
Does this mean AI is "over" or today's stock market crash marks "the end?" Absolutely not.
Rather, we believe we are witnessing a sudden shift in sentiment colliding with excessive levels of leverage, potentially triggering forced liquidations by several major institutional investors.
Therefore, today's downturn is more technical than fundamental. This is not to discount the concerns around regulation, they are legitimate. But price action right now does not look orderly or rational.
We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in human history.
Zoom out and remain calm.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Inflation has more than wiped out all US consumer wage gains since the 2020 Pandemic: US consumer p...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Inflation has more than wiped out all US consumer wage gains since the 2020 Pandemic:
US consumer prices have risen +31.3% since April 2020, to an all-time high in September.
Over the same period, average hourly earnings have increased just +25.9%.
This comes as CPI inflation has now been above the Fed’s 2% target for 67 consecutive months, the 3rd-longest streak over the last 100 years.
The only 2 longer streaks lasted 242 months, ending in 1986, and 128 months, ending in 1997.
Inflation continues to erode the spending power of Americans.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: South Korea's exports surged +94% YoY in October, to $115 billion, the 2nd-highest readin...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: South Korea's exports surged +94% YoY in October, to $115 billion, the 2nd-highest reading on record.
This also marks the strongest YoY growth since January 1974.
South Korea’s exports have now recorded 5 consecutive months with YoY growth of at least +60%.
In the first 10 months of 2026, exports totaled a record $930 billion.
Semiconductors led last month's surge, rising +259% YoY, to a record $56 billion.
At the same time, computer sales spiked +497% amid strong demand for AI servers.
The AI boom has turned South Korea into an export powerhouse.
item.content:encoded:
BREAKING: South Korea's exports surged +94% YoY in October, to $115 billion, the 2nd-highest reading on record.

This also marks the strongest YoY growth since January 1974.

South Korea’s exports have now recorded 5 consecutive months with YoY growth of at least +60%.

In the first 10 months of 2026, exports totaled a record $930 billion.

Semiconductors led last month's surge, rising +259% YoY, to a record $56 billion.

At the same time, computer sales spiked +497% amid strong demand for AI servers.

The AI boom has turned South Korea into an export powerhouse.

item.title: @wallstengine: Goldman Sachs $GS and Apollo $APO are approaching Wall Street investors to sell portions of SpaceX...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Goldman Sachs $GS and Apollo $APO are approaching Wall Street investors to sell portions of SpaceX $SPCX's roughly $40B AI chip financing deal.
The two firms have begun marketing the financing to potential buyers, with some investors being offered portions worth as much as $500M ahead of the formal syndication process, which is expected to begin soon.
The financing, announced in October, is the largest GPU financing arrangement on record.
Here's how the deal is structured:
An Apollo-backed entity will purchase approximately $47.3B worth of Nvidia GPUs and related equipment, primarily its next-generation Rubin chips.
The purchases will be financed through roughly $40B in debt, alongside a $7B lease prepayment from SpaceX.
SpaceX will then lease the chips for approximately five years, using a structure designed to keep the financing debt off its own balance sheet and protect its credit ratings.
The debt package includes an $8.3B senior-secured loan, alongside multiple bond tranches being marketed to institutional investors.
The Nvidia chips are expected to be delivered in the first half of 2027.
One interesting detail is that SpaceX's rental obligations remain unconditional.
The company must continue making payments even if the equipment is damaged or extraordinary events disrupt operations. SpaceX also isn't providing a guarantee covering the chips' residual value at the end of the lease.
Source: Bloomberg

The two firms have begun marketing the financing to potential buyers, with some investors being offered portions worth as much as $500M ahead of the formal syndication process, which is expected to begin soon.

The financing, announced in October, is the largest GPU financing arrangement on record.

An Apollo-backed entity will purchase approximately $47.3B worth of Nvidia GPUs and related equipment, primarily its next-generation Rubin chips.

The purchases will be financed through roughly $40B in debt, alongside a $7B lease prepayment from SpaceX.

SpaceX will then lease the chips for approximately five years, using a structure designed to keep the financing debt off its own balance sheet and protect its credit ratings.

The debt package includes an $8.3B senior-secured loan, alongside multiple bond tranches being marketed to institutional investors.

The Nvidia chips are expected to be delivered in the first half of 2027.

One interesting detail is that SpaceX's rental obligations remain unconditional.

The company must continue making payments even if the equipment is damaged or extraordinary events disrupt operations. SpaceX also isn't providing a guarantee covering the chips' residual value at the end of the lease.

Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The era of massive Big Tech stock buybacks is over. Combined buybacks by Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon,...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The era of massive Big Tech stock buybacks is over.
Combined buybacks by Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, Microsoft, $MSFT, Meta, $META, and Oracle, $ORCL, fell to $4.4 billion in Q3 2026, the lowest since Q3 2017.
Share repurchases have dropped -90% since the ~$45.9 billion peak recorded in Q4 2021.
This also marks the 3rd consecutive quarter with buybacks below $5.0 billion.
This comes as Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle have not purchased their own stock in 2026.
By comparison, combined buybacks by these Big Tech companies stood at +$33.0 billion in Q1 2026.
AI spending is coming at the expense of Big Tech buybacks.

item.title: @Hedgeye: McCullough: This Hike Will Look Like A Policy Mistake 🔊 On the Free Edition of The Macro Show this...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
McCullough: This Hike Will Look Like A Policy Mistake
🔊
On the Free Edition of The Macro Show this morning, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough covered why the Fed is set up for a policy mistake.
Inflation reports lag the economy, and the next couple are still ticking up, which gives the Fed cover to raise rates in December.
As Keith put it, that hike “is going to look like a policy mistake,” because it lands just as the AI bubble and the credit tied to it start to crack.
Raising rates into a slowdown is how a wobble becomes a panic, and when that panic hits, the Fed does what it always does, cuts rates, which only makes it worse.
The tell is in the bond market.
Longer-term yields are already falling because they see growth and inflation slowing ahead.
Keith also flagged the timing, the last major cycle peaked in October 2007, the same month he was fired from Carlyle for being too bearish, right before the crash.
Watch the full episode of The Macro Show here: https://app.hedgeye.com/insights/189400-watch-for-free-the-macro-show-markets-midterms-the-road-to-quad?type=macro%2Cmarket-insights

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: This is highly unusual: The S&P 500 is trading more than 2 standard deviations below its 50-day mov...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
This is highly unusual:
The S&P 500 is trading more than 2 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, the first such occurrence since April.
Such a reading puts the S&P 500 in historically extreme oversold territory.
At the same time, only ~17% of the index’s stocks are now oversold, near its lowest proportion since July.
Meanwhile, ~47% of stocks are now overbought, the highest proportion since early February.
This figure has more than doubled since the start of October as many stocks have rallied beneath the surface.
The broader market looks far healthier than the S&P 500's recent performance suggests.

1. Iran War 2. Cost of living and inflation 3. Voters want "America First" 4. Relationship with Israel

US oil prices are falling sharply after Vance's remarks.

item.title: @Hedgeye: "These walls are funny. First you hate 'em. Then you get used to 'em. Enough time passes, you get s...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
"These walls are funny. First you hate 'em. Then you get used to 'em. Enough time passes, you get so you depend on 'em." - Red, The Shawshank Redemption
Same goes for bubbles.
First you hate getting squeezed by one. Then you start buying the damn dips in it. Enough time passes, you depend on it.
Then the walls close in.
That's how the Macro Tourist gets institutionalized. Every bubble. Every cycle.
Andy Dufresne didn't wait for the walls to close before he started digging. He had a plan years ahead of time.
Yours can be a lot simpler than a rock hammer and a poster. Know your MAX size before you buy. Know your TRADE and TREND lines. Know exactly what you do when both break.

item.title: @wallstengine: Oracle $ORCL has reportedly canceled a $7B AI chip leasing deal with Tencent following pressure fro...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Oracle $ORCL has reportedly canceled a $7B AI chip leasing deal with Tencent following pressure from the Trump administration, according to the FT.
The five-year agreement would have given Tencent access to as many as 100,000 advanced AI chips across Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia, making it Tencent's largest overseas chip leasing deal.
The arrangement would have allowed Tencent to use advanced computing hardware unavailable inside China because of U.S. and Chinese restrictions.
U.S. officials reportedly approached Oracle with concerns about the agreement. Meanwhile, senior Chinese officials visited Tencent and urged the company to support domestic chipmakers.
Although overseas AI chip leasing remains permitted under existing rules, the deal has now been canceled following pressure from both Washington and Beijing.
Oracle, Tencent, and the White House have not publicly commented on the reported cancellation.

item.title: @wallstengine: TEXAS TURNS BLUE IN A HISTORIC DOUBLE FLIP Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseats Gov. Greg Abbott, becomin...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TEXAS TURNS BLUE IN A HISTORIC DOUBLE FLIP
Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseats Gov. Greg Abbott, becoming Texas's first Democratic governor since Ann Richards was elected in 1990.
Democrat James Talarico also defeats Ken Paxton in the U.S. Senate race, marking the first Democratic Senate victory in Texas since 1988.
This ends Republicans' 32-year winning streak in Texas statewide elections.
The outcome could also have major implications for Texas's AI data center boom and ERCOT's power grid.
Hinojosa has called for a moratorium on new data center development, stricter power and water regulations, and an end to data center tax breaks.
Jefferies estimates that a Hinojosa victory could put 13.1 GW of announced Texas data center projects at immediate risk.
item.content:encoded:
TEXAS TURNS BLUE IN A HISTORIC DOUBLE FLIP

Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseats Gov. Greg Abbott, becoming Texas's first Democratic governor since Ann Richards was elected in 1990.

Democrat James Talarico also defeats Ken Paxton in the U.S. Senate race, marking the first Democratic Senate victory in Texas since 1988.

This ends Republicans' 32-year winning streak in Texas statewide elections.

The outcome could also have major implications for Texas's AI data center boom and ERCOT's power grid.

Hinojosa has called for a moratorium on new data center development, stricter power and water regulations, and an end to data center tax breaks.

Jefferies estimates that a Hinojosa victory could put 13.1 GW of announced Texas data center projects at immediate risk.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US federal debt surged +$422 billion in October, to a record $40.6 trillion. Since July 1...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US federal debt surged +$422 billion in October, to a record $40.6 trillion.
Since July 1st alone, US federal debt has soared +$1.2 trillion, averaging +$300 billion per month.
This is equivalent to an increase of ~$10 billion per day.
As a result, the US total public Debt-to-GDP ratio is up to 123%, the highest since the 2020 pandemic peak.
Meanwhile, the Treasury borrowed a record $839 billion through auctions of Treasury bills and notes last week, with the majority going toward repaying holders of maturing bills.

item.content:encoded:

Since July 1st alone, US federal debt has soared +$1.2 trillion, averaging +$300 billion per month.

This is equivalent to an increase of ~$10 billion per day.

As a result, the US total public Debt-to-GDP ratio is up to 123%, the highest since the 2020 pandemic peak.

Meanwhile, the Treasury borrowed a record $839 billion through auctions of Treasury bills and notes last week, with the majority going toward repaying holders of maturing bills.

This surpassed the previous all-time high of $834 billion set during the same period in 2025.

The US debt crisis is in full-swing.

item.title: @wallstengine: $ANET +18% JUST POSTED ITS FASTEST REVENUE GROWTH SINCE GOING PUBLIC IN 2014, UP 58.5% YOY. Arista...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$ANET +18%
JUST POSTED ITS FASTEST REVENUE GROWTH SINCE GOING PUBLIC IN 2014, UP 58.5% YOY.
Arista beat Wall Street expectations in Q3 and guided Q4 above estimates, while introducing a 2027 outlook well ahead of expectations.
Despite ramping investments in AI networking, liquid cooling, and high-speed switching, Arista delivered a 49.1% adjusted operating margin.
The company also raised its 2026 revenue guidance for the fourth time this year to $13.3B, representing 48% annual growth.
Looking ahead to 2027, management expects approximately $18.5B in revenue, or 38%-40% growth. That's well above the roughly $16.4B analysts were modeling before earnings.
AI networking is expected to drive much of that growth.
Arista expects its AI fabrics business to approximately double from at least $3.5B in 2026 to around $7B in 2027, accounting for nearly 38% of total company revenue next year.
Meanwhile, its campus networking business is projected to grow 60% to approximately $2B.
CEO Jayshree Ullal said Arista has now surpassed 100 Etherlink customers, compared with just four or five major AI customers when the company began its AI networking push a few years ago.
By the end of 2027, Arista expects more than 10 gigawatts of AI deployments across at least 10 different types of compute accelerators.
Another interesting development is the shift from centralized AI training toward distributed inference, where different parts of a workload, including prefill and token generation, run across separate systems.
That requires more networking capacity and more intelligent routing between GPUs, memory, and storage. Arista sees this as another growth opportunity beyond traditional AI data center networking.
The company is also expanding into scale-up Ethernet, which connects accelerators within and across racks, with customer trials expected in 2027 and production targeted for 2028.
item.content:encoded:
$ANET +18%

JUST POSTED ITS FASTEST REVENUE GROWTH SINCE GOING PUBLIC IN 2014, UP 58.5% YOY.

Arista beat Wall Street expectations in Q3 and guided Q4 above estimates, while introducing a 2027 outlook well ahead of expectations.

Despite ramping investments in AI networking, liquid cooling, and high-speed switching, Arista delivered a 49.1% adjusted operating margin.

The company also raised its 2026 revenue guidance for the fourth time this year to $13.3B, representing 48% annual growth.

Looking ahead to 2027, management expects approximately $18.5B in revenue, or 38%-40% growth. That's well above the roughly $16.4B analysts were modeling before earnings.

AI networking is expected to drive much of that growth.

Arista expects its AI fabrics business to approximately double from at least $3.5B in 2026 to around $7B in 2027, accounting for nearly 38% of total company revenue next year.

Meanwhile, its campus networking business is projected to grow 60% to approximately $2B.

CEO Jayshree Ullal said Arista has now surpassed 100 Etherlink customers, compared with just four or five major AI customers when the company began its AI networking push a few years ago.

By the end of 2027, Arista expects more than 10 gigawatts of AI deployments across at least 10 different types of compute accelerators.

Another interesting development is the shift from centralized AI training toward distributed inference, where different parts of a workload, including prefill and token generation, run across separate systems.

That requires more networking capacity and more intelligent routing between GPUs, memory, and storage. Arista sees this as another growth opportunity beyond traditional AI data center networking.

The company is also expanding into scale-up Ethernet, which connects accelerators within and across racks, with customer trials expected in 2027 and production targeted for 2028.

item.title: @wallstengine: $AMD RECORDED A $1.1B NON-CASH CHARGE TIED TO ITS OPENAI & META WARRANTS DEALS IN Q3 Buried in AMD'...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AMD RECORDED A $1.1B NON-CASH CHARGE TIED TO ITS OPENAI & META WARRANTS DEALS IN Q3
Buried in AMD's Q3 earnings reconciliation is a $1.097B change in the fair value of customer warrants, reducing GAAP EPS by $0.66.
Here's how it works.
Under its AI deals, OpenAI and Meta each received warrants to buy up to 160 million AMD shares at just $0.01 per share, or 320 million shares combined.
The warrants vest as customers meet GPU purchase commitments and AMD achieves specified stock-price milestones.
AMD must revalue these warrants every quarter based on its stock price and other assumptions. As their value increases, AMD records an accounting expense.
So the $1.1B charge wasn't cash paid to customers, but it was the largest single adjustment between AMD's $2.43B GAAP net income and $3.47B adjusted net income.
The other thing worth watching is the potential shareholder dilution if those warrants eventually vest and are exercised.
item.content:encoded:
$AMD RECORDED A $1.1B NON-CASH CHARGE TIED TO ITS OPENAI & META WARRANTS DEALS IN Q3

Buried in AMD's Q3 earnings reconciliation is a $1.097B change in the fair value of customer warrants, reducing GAAP EPS by $0.66.

Here's how it works.

Under its AI deals, OpenAI and Meta each received warrants to buy up to 160 million AMD shares at just $0.01 per share, or 320 million shares combined.

The warrants vest as customers meet GPU purchase commitments and AMD achieves specified stock-price milestones.

AMD must revalue these warrants every quarter based on its stock price and other assumptions. As their value increases, AMD records an accounting expense.

So the $1.1B charge wasn't cash paid to customers, but it was the largest single adjustment between AMD's $2.43B GAAP net income and $3.47B adjusted net income.

The other thing worth watching is the potential shareholder dilution if those warrants eventually vest and are exercised.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investors are rushing into Treasuries: The ratio of the Nasdaq 100 to the 20+ Year Treasury Bond ET...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investors are rushing into Treasuries:
The ratio of the Nasdaq 100 to the 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF, $TLT, is down to 342.5, its lowest since July 31st.
Since the all-time high recorded on October 7th, this ratio has fallen -15.4%.
Over this period, $TLT has risen +7.1%, while the Nasdaq 100 has fallen -10.2%.
This puts the ratio on track for its 5th consecutive weekly decline, its longest losing streak since the 2022 bear market.
Similar sharp drops in this metric were also recorded between February and April 2025 and during the 2020 pandemic.
Investors are buying bonds to protect against an AI selloff.

In 27 early-voting states that track voter registration by party, ~43% of early votes were by registered Democrats and ~32% by registered Republicans.
The first polls will close at 6 PM ET with the last polls closing at 1 AM ET.
Turn on our post notifications at @KobeissiLetter for real-time analysis as the day progresses.

item.description:
McCullough: A Volatility Regime Shift Is Underway
🔊
Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough covered what happens to markets when volatility shifts regimes on The Macro Show this morning.
The framework comes from the fractals that back-test across every Quad 4 Keith has called.
When an asset goes bearish TRADE and bearish TREND and enters a volatility regime shift, it moves from the investable bucket into the chop bucket, which is where the S&P 500 sits now.
The next step down is the worst bucket, and that’s where the Nasdaq already is, down -9%.
That’s a drawdown but not a crash, and Keith said he’d be shocked if the Nasdaq isn’t down more than 20% by the time the market reaches the throat of Quad 4, the really bad part, by Q2 of next year.
With Q4 nearly over, the market is starting to discount Q1. The warning for bulls is in the price action.
Futures bouncing, getting sold, then bouncing again doesn’t calm volatility, it amplifies the signal.
As Keith put it, “that’s fractal math. Those are the fractals. They know.”

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: It's officially election day. History says stocks are heading higher. In fact, the S&P 500 has clos...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
It's officially election day.
History says stocks are heading higher.
In fact, the S&P 500 has closed GREEN in the year following every US Midterm election since 1980.
As we noted in our analysis yesterday, we believe recent weakness in markets is largely a function of the uncertainty around Midterm elections.
However, when this uncertainty dissipates, markets react positively.
Since 1980, the S&P 500 has averaged a +14% gain in the 12 months following US Midterm elections.
Furthermore, even after divided-government outcomes, the index has averaged a +15% one-year gain, compared to +12% under single-party control.
Of course, the near-term picture will come with volatility and change.
But, if history is any guide, it's a great time to be bullish.
Turn on our post notifications at @KobeissiLetter for real-time analysis as this develops.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US semiconductor stocks have rarely been this volatile:
Over the last 5 mins S&P 500 Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment Index has recorded 11 trading sessions in which at least 50% of its components fell -5% or more, the 4th-highest reading on record.
By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, the index recorded 16 such sessions.
The only other periods with more volatility were 2000 and 2002, following the Dot-Com Bubble burst.
Furthermore, the S&P 500 Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment Index fell more than -5% on 12 trading days over the last 5 months.
The index is now down -32% from its June peak, trading at its lowest level since April.
Semiconductor stocks are experiencing historic volatility.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI infrastructure spending is driving a sharp increase in US bank lending: Commercial and Industria...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI infrastructure spending is driving a sharp increase in US bank lending:
Commercial and Industrial (C&I) loans at large US banks surged +11.4% YoY in October, to $1.6 trillion, the most since June 2020.
This also marked their largest YoY growth since February 2023.
In Q3, C&I loans at the 25 largest US banks grew almost +10.0% YoY, the strongest growth in 10 years excluding pandemic-related swings.
This represents a sharp reversal from an -8.0% YoY contraction in Q4 2025.
The surge has been driven by rising borrowing demand from Big Tech companies and data-center developers to fund AI infrastructure projects.
At the same time, regional lenders are providing credit to construction companies and other businesses benefiting from the investment boom.
The data-center buildout is increasingly being funded by debt.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, and Oracle, $ORCL, have n...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, and Oracle, $ORCL, have now disclosed a record $3.3 trillion in future spending commitments.
These are off-balance-sheet commitments covering data-center spending, future equipment purchases, leases, and other obligations.
$GOOGL accounts for the largest amount at $1.06 trillion, with its disclosed commitments surging nearly +700% over the last year.
$META follows at $866 billion, with nearly half tied to data-center leases that have not yet commenced and payment periods extending up to 30 years.
Meanwhile, Microsoft, $MSFT, has $593 billion in commitments, followed by Amazon, $AMZN, at $453 billion, and Oracle, $ORCL, at $322 billion.
The AI infrastructure buildout is creating an unprecedented pipeline of future financial obligations.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Leverage is skyrocketing in this market: US leveraged ETFs have attracted +$15 billion in inflows o...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Leverage is skyrocketing in this market:
US leveraged ETFs have attracted +$15 billion in inflows over the last month, their largest 1-month rolling inflow in at least 2 years.
This marks a sharp reversal from -$2 billion seen in early October.
By comparison, during the April 2025 market recovery, this figure peaked at +$12 billion.
The surge has been primarily led by retail investor demand for leveraged tech equity ETFs.
The 3x leveraged long Semiconductor ETF, $SOXL, alone attracted +$7.3 billion in October, its largest monthly inflow on record.
Retail investors are aggressively piling into leveraged equity ETFs.

item.description:
OPENAI HIRES FORMER U.S. ARMY SECRETARY: FT
Dan Driscoll will join OpenAI as senior counselor for national security modernization, helping the company expand AI adoption across U.S. and allied defense institutions.
An Iraq War veteran and close friend of Vice President JD Vance, Driscoll previously pushed to accelerate military technology adoption before resigning amid tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The appointment follows OpenAI's recent agreement to deploy its AI models in classified Pentagon environments after the military's negotiations with Anthropic broke down.
item.content:encoded:
OPENAI HIRES FORMER U.S. ARMY SECRETARY: FT

Dan Driscoll will join OpenAI as senior counselor for national security modernization, helping the company expand AI adoption across U.S. and allied defense institutions.

An Iraq War veteran and close friend of Vice President JD Vance, Driscoll previously pushed to accelerate military technology adoption before resigning amid tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

The appointment follows OpenAI's recent agreement to deploy its AI models in classified Pentagon environments after the military's negotiations with Anthropic broke down.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: What's happening now in the stock market is more than just a "correction in tech stocks." Sure, AI...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
What's happening now in the stock market is more than just a "correction in tech stocks."
Sure, AI CapEx concerns are legitimate and investors will always care about profitability.
But, there's more beneath the surface here.
The reality is that the market is pricing-in a major shift in the political landscape of the US.
Over the last 12 months, market expectations for a Democrat "sweep" of the US Midterm elections have tripled.
Over the last 45 days alone, these expectations are up +30 percentage points.
As it stands, markets themselves now see a near-80% chance of a Democrat "sweep" of the US Midterm elections.
President Trump has already vowed to become "Mr. Veto" if this in fact does happen.
This is post is not political, it's objective. A change in the political landscape always comes with uncertainty; markets hate uncertainty.
Objectively, the market is in the process of pricing-in two years of political gridlock.
Could this change? Of course. But markets price-in the most probable outcome, and the odds now overwhelmingly favor the aforementioned scenario.
Tomorrow sets the stage for the next two years.

item.title: @wallstengine: PALANTIR SHOWS FINE-TUNED NVIDIA 4B AI MODEL BEATING GPT-6 ASTRA & CLAUDE SONNET 5.5 AT A FRACTION...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
PALANTIR SHOWS FINE-TUNED NVIDIA 4B AI MODEL BEATING GPT-6 ASTRA & CLAUDE SONNET 5.5 AT A FRACTION OF THE COST
In its Q3 business update, $PLTR revealed that a fine-tuned $NVDA Nemotron 3 Nano model with just 4 billion parameters outperformed much larger frontier models on a real-world customer task.
The results, based on classifying requests for information for construction firm McCarthy:
• NVIDIA Nemotron 4B: ~75% accuracy at $0.10 per million tokens.
• Claude Sonnet 5.5: ~66% accuracy at $4 per million tokens.
• GPT-6 Astra: ~62% accuracy at $20 per million tokens.
Palantir says the fine-tuned models are expected to save McCarthy approximately 30,000 drafting hours annually.
Separately, NVIDIA itself is now training open AI models on its own supply chain data inside Palantir's Ontology, spanning millions of parts and thousands of suppliers.
Jensen Huang says the partnership combines NVIDIA's Nemotron models with Palantir's Ontology to:
“Reason, plan and orchestrate the journey from wafer to token.”

item.title: @wallstengine: BLOOM ENERGY $BE & CALIFORNIA RESOURCES SIGN DEAL TO EXPLORE 1 GW+ OF POWER GENERATION IN CALIFORNI...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
BLOOM ENERGY $BE & CALIFORNIA RESOURCES SIGN DEAL TO EXPLORE 1 GW+ OF POWER GENERATION IN CALIFORNIA
The companies signed a non-binding MOU to develop solid-oxide fuel cell projects paired with carbon capture and storage.
Bloom would supply its fuel cell technology, while CRC's Carbon TerraVault would provide CO2 transportation and permanent storage.
The projects, being considered in Central and Northern California, could serve data centers, utilities and industrial customers.
The companies estimate up to 3 million metric tons of CO2 annually could be available for capture and storage.
Development remains subject to final agreements, investment decisions and regulatory approvals.

Major institutional investors are reportedly urging Anthropic to pursue a more conservative IPO valuation of $1.5T to $1.6T, well below the roughly $2T valuation discussed in recent months.
Some investors reportedly favor a lower starting valuation to leave room for a strong first-day trading gain, with expectations that Anthropic could potentially reach a $2T valuation after its market debut.

Anthropic is expected to begin its IPO roadshow as soon as next week, with its Nasdaq debut targeted for the week before Thanksgiving.

item.title: @HedgeyeENERGY: Introducing the Hedgeye Oil Model. We built a fair-value model for WTI based on global oil inventor...
item.dc:creator: @HedgeyeENERGY
item.description:
Introducing the Hedgeye Oil Model.
We built a fair-value model for WTI based on global oil inventories. Since 2011, it explains about 80% of WTI's price moves.
What it says today:
- WTI fair value is about $91 a barrel, with a ±$10 band. - WTI is $96 after today's 8% drop on Iran talks. That's inside the band. - The war premium peaked at $22 over fair value in March to May. - WTI then traded $2 to $5 below fair value in June to August as the market looked through the disruption. - The premium came back this fall, at about $7 in September and $11 in October. - For fair value to reach $105, OECD inventories need to draw about another 100 million barrels. At this year's pace, that's four to six months away. - On EIA's current estimates, fair value holds near $90 through year-end. If inventories rebuild in 2027 as EIA expects, fair value falls into the $60s by mid-2027.
Bottom line: on inventories, oil is fairly priced. The upside case needs more draws, not more headlines.
We'll update the model regularly as new inventory data comes in.
item.content:encoded:
Introducing the Hedgeye Oil Model.

We built a fair-value model for WTI based on global oil inventories. Since 2011, it explains about 80% of WTI's price moves.

What it says today:

- WTI fair value is about $91 a barrel, with a ±$10 band.
- WTI is $96 after today's 8% drop on Iran talks. That's inside the band.
- The war premium peaked at $22 over fair value in March to May.
- WTI then traded $2 to $5 below fair value in June to August as the market looked through the disruption.
- The premium came back this fall, at about $7 in September and $11 in October.
- For fair value to reach $105, OECD inventories need to draw about another 100 million barrels. At this year's pace, that's four to six months away.
- On EIA's current estimates, fair value holds near $90 through year-end. If inventories rebuild in 2027 as EIA expects, fair value falls into the $60s by mid-2027.

Bottom line: on inventories, oil is fairly priced. The upside case needs more draws, not more headlines.

We'll update the model regularly as new inventory data comes in.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US equity funds recorded -$6.7 billion in outflows in the week ending October 28th, their largest weekly withdrawal since mid-September.
This follows +$5.1 billion and +$13.0 billion in inflows over the previous two weeks.
Meanwhile, global equity funds attracted +$10.2 billion in the week ending October 28th, marking their 6th consecutive weekly intake.
However, this was down from +$25.1 billion and +$19.8 billion in the preceding two weeks.
Asian equity funds led last week's inflows, attracting +$9.9 billion, compared with +$11.6 billion the previous week.
At the same time, European equity funds attracted +$4.5 billion.
Global investors are rotating out of US equities into other regions.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Markets are heading into their strongest seasonal period of the year: Since 1980, the S&P 500 has r...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Markets are heading into their strongest seasonal period of the year:
Since 1980, the S&P 500 has rallied +2.1% on average in November, making it the strongest month of the year.
Over this period, positive returns occurred 74% of the time, the best hit rate of any month.
Furthermore, the S&P 500 has gained +1.6% on average in November since 1964, with positive returns occurring 69% of the time.
The highest November return during this period was +10.8%, recorded in 2020.
During midterm years, November has averaged +2.7% since 1950, with a 78.9% win rate.
History points to a strong month ahead.

Keith added $BNDD, a disinflation ETF, to position for falling long-term bond yields.

item.description:
Tokenization is the biggest bull market in crypto.
The total circulating supply of onchain tokenized equities just hit another record high, at $3.8 billion.
This metric has now reached a new record high for 10 consecutive weeks, up +590% year-to-date.
It has become increasingly clear that financial markets are moving toward tokenizing everything.
Investors are demanding 24/7 markets, and tokenized assets are increasingly fulfilling that demand.
Amid the shift, Jupiter, the largest onchain platform on Solana, reported that 70% of tokenized asset trading now occurs outside traditional market hours.
Amid this surge in demand, the NYSE is developing infrastructure for tokenized equities and perpetual futures.
The future of financial markets is onchain.

item.title: @wallstengine: HUME LAUNCHES AN API THAT ANALYZES HOW PEOPLE SOUND A confident “sure” and a hesitant “…sure” can l...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
HUME LAUNCHES AN API THAT ANALYZES HOW PEOPLE SOUND
A confident “sure” and a hesitant “…sure” can look identical in a transcript. Hume’s Decision API analyzes the recording itself, including tone, pauses and interruptions.
Developers provide: • An audio clip • A question, such as “Does the caller sound unsure?” • Possible answers
The API returns a probability for each answer, trained to reflect how human listeners would respond.
Those scores could help voice-agent teams decide when to ask for clarification, review a call or assess how naturally their agent responds.
https://x.com/hume_ai/status/2117285608745820372/video/1
item.content:encoded:
HUME LAUNCHES AN API THAT ANALYZES HOW PEOPLE SOUND

A confident “sure” and a hesitant “…sure” can look identical in a transcript. Hume’s Decision API analyzes the recording itself, including tone, pauses and interruptions.

Developers provide:
• An audio clip
• A question, such as “Does the caller sound unsure?”
• Possible answers

The API returns a probability for each answer, trained to reflect how human listeners would respond.

Those scores could help voice-agent teams decide when to ask for clarification, review a call or assess how naturally their agent responds.

item.title: @wallstengine: OpenAI announced its new Grid Protectors program, designed to reduce electricity use at future AI d...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OpenAI announced its new Grid Protectors program, designed to reduce electricity use at future AI data centers when local power grids are strained.
Its planned Georgia campus is expected to require 3.2GW of power, but could reduce demand by up to 1GW during peak periods, equivalent to the average electricity use of roughly 700,000 homes.
The campus is still in development.
OpenAI says it will cover the full electricity and grid infrastructure costs.

item.title: @wallstengine: $MRVL TO ACQUIRE $LITE IN $115B ALL-STOCK DEAL Marvell has agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-sto...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$MRVL TO ACQUIRE $LITE IN $115B ALL-STOCK DEAL
Marvell has agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $115B in enterprise value, combining two major suppliers of AI infrastructure and optical networking technology.
Under the agreement:
• Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each LITE share, implying roughly $1,132 per share.
• The offer represents a 23.9% premium to unaffected closing prices on October 28.
• Marvell shareholders will own approximately 67% of the combined company, with Lumentum shareholders holding 33%.
The deal brings together Marvell's custom AI chips, networking switches and interconnect technology with Lumentum's lasers, optical transceivers and optical circuit switching capabilities.
The bigger opportunity is the growing shift from copper to optical connectivity as AI data centers require faster data transfer, greater bandwidth and improved power efficiency.
Marvell says the combination could expand its addressable market to $550B, allowing it to offer more integrated connectivity solutions across AI data centers and within advanced chip packages.
The companies also expect:
• More than $1B in annual run-rate cost synergies.
• Improved long-term revenue growth and profit margins.
• Accretion to Marvell's adjusted EPS in the first year after closing.
Matt Murphy will remain CEO of the combined company, with the transaction expected to close in H1 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
Separately, Marvell reaffirmed the midpoint of its fiscal Q3 revenue guidance while narrowing the expected range to ±2% from ±5%.
item.content:encoded:
$MRVL TO ACQUIRE $LITE IN $115B ALL-STOCK DEAL

Marvell has agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $115B in enterprise value, combining two major suppliers of AI infrastructure and optical networking technology.

Under the agreement:

• Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each LITE share, implying roughly $1,132 per share.

• The offer represents a 23.9% premium to unaffected closing prices on October 28.

• Marvell shareholders will own approximately 67% of the combined company, with Lumentum shareholders holding 33%.

The deal brings together Marvell's custom AI chips, networking switches and interconnect technology with Lumentum's lasers, optical transceivers and optical circuit switching capabilities.

The bigger opportunity is the growing shift from copper to optical connectivity as AI data centers require faster data transfer, greater bandwidth and improved power efficiency.

Marvell says the combination could expand its addressable market to $550B, allowing it to offer more integrated connectivity solutions across AI data centers and within advanced chip packages.

The companies also expect:

• More than $1B in annual run-rate cost synergies.

• Improved long-term revenue growth and profit margins.

• Accretion to Marvell's adjusted EPS in the first year after closing.

Matt Murphy will remain CEO of the combined company, with the transaction expected to close in H1 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

Separately, Marvell reaffirmed the midpoint of its fiscal Q3 revenue guidance while narrowing the expected range to ±2% from ±5%.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US healthcare costs are rising at an alarming rate: Medical care prices have surged +132% since 200...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US healthcare costs are rising at an alarming rate:
Medical care prices have surged +132% since 2000, the largest increase among major consumer spending categories.
Over the same period, shelter costs have risen +127%, while food prices have soared +112%.
Price increases across all these spending categories have outpaced overall CPI, which is up +99% since 2000.
As a result, ~30% of insured US adults have skipped or delayed getting healthcare they needed due to costs over the last 12 months, according to a KFF survey.
Healthcare costs have never been higher.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The global copper market is extremely tight: China's copper import premium over London Metal Exchan...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The global copper market is extremely tight:
China's copper import premium over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices has surpassed $200 per ton, the largest premium on record.
The Yangshan premium, named after a Shanghai port that serves as a major hub for Chinese copper imports, has more than doubled over the last 3 months.
Since the beginning of 2026, this figure has surged +700%.
Furthermore, the premium of spot prices over three-month futures on the LME widened to $217 per ton, the largest since mid-August.
This has been driven by strong Chinese copper demand and domestic inventories falling below typical seasonal levels.
At the same time, expectations of potential US tariffs on refined copper have redirected hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US, leaving global inventories heavily concentrated in the country.
The physical copper supply squeeze is far from over.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: South Korea’s economy grew +1.0% QoQ in Q3 2026, marking its 3rd consecutive quarterly expansion, beating expectations of +0.8%.
Exports were the main driver, rising +2.3% on stronger semiconductor, machinery and electrical equipment shipments.
Facility investment surged +4.1%, particularly reflecting increased spending on machinery, including semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
YoY, South Korea's economy grew +3.4%, exceeding expectations of +3.0% and following +3.7% and +3.8% growth in Q2 and Q3, respectively.
South Korea is now on track to surpass $1 trillion in annual exports for the first time in 2026, making it only the 4th economy after the US, China, and Germany to reach this threshold.
South Korea is seeing a historic economic transformation.

AI spending is rapidly accelerating in the US.
US private fixed investment in information processing equipment and software grew at an annualized rate of +7.3% in Q3 2026, to a record $1.77 trillion.
This marks the largest quarterly increase since Q4 1983.
By comparison, at the height of the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, this metric grew +6.2%.
Since Q4 2022, private fixed investment in information processing equipment and software has surged +61%, or +$671 billion.
As a % of GDP, this metric is up to a record 5.4%, significantly surpassing the previous high of 4.5% recorded in Q4 2000.
The scale of US AI investment is unlike anything seen before.

Imports rose +$8.1 billion, or +2.4%, to a record $344.2 billion.
This jump was led by a +7.5% MoM increase in capital goods, which include computers and accessories, semiconductors, and telecommunications equipment fueling the AI buildout.
Now, the capital goods deficit has widened by -$54.3 billion YoY, accounting for more than the entire increase in the overall trade deficit.
Meanwhile, US goods exports jumped +$5.3 billion in September, or +2.6%, to $209.2 billion, driven by a +12.8% increase in food shipments.
The US trade deficit is rapidly widening again.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI is burning Big Tech's free cash flow: The combined CapEx of Amazon, $AMZN, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Met...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI is burning Big Tech's free cash flow:
The combined CapEx of Amazon, $AMZN, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, and Microsoft, $MSFT, rose +$36.9 billion in Q3 2026, to a record $201.9 billion.
This figure has more than doubled over the last 12 months and is up +356% since Q1 2024.
Big Tech has now spent $1.6 trillion on CapEx over the last 3 years.
Meanwhile, the combined free cash flow of these companies fell -$33.1 billion last quarter, to -$26.4 billion, its lowest on record.
Free cash flow among these firms has dropped -$88.2 billion over the last year.
Only Microsoft reported positive free cash flow in Q3.
Looking ahead, these 4 companies plan to spend another $232 billion on CapEx in Q4, potentially lifting their combined CapEx to a record $740 billion in 2026.
Big Tech is undertaking one of the largest infrastructure buildouts in history.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US companies are facing a massive debt maturity wall: ~$1.9 trillion in US speculative-grade corpor...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US companies are facing a massive debt maturity wall:
~$1.9 trillion in US speculative-grade corporate bonds and loans mature over the next 5 years, including $438 billion due by the end of 2028.
By comparison, in 2020, 2021, and 2022, this figure ranged from $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion.
The amount of junk-rated debt maturing within 2 years alone has surged +31% YoY.
At the same time, $1.6 trillion of investment-grade corporate debt is coming due by 2031.
Meanwhile, refinancing is becoming increasingly expensive, with the effective yield on publicly issued US junk debt rising +150 basis points over the last 12 months, to 8.0%.
The corporate refinancing burden is becoming a major issue.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US personal savings rate fell -0.2 percentage points in September, to 4.2%, its lowes...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US personal savings rate fell -0.2 percentage points in September, to 4.2%, its lowest level since October 2022.
Since January 2024, this metric has declined -3.4 percentage points.
The personal savings rate is now well below the 5-year pre-pandemic average of 6.2%.
This comes as personal income grew +4.1% YoY in September, its 2nd-lowest growth rate since April 2022.
At the same time, personal consumption expenditures rose +6.3% YoY, the 2nd-highest YoY growth since December 2024.
In other words, consumer spending continues to outpace income growth, putting further pressure on household savings and increasing household reliance on borrowing.
Elevated inflation and record prices are putting further pressure on consumer savings.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US corporate debt issuance is skyrocketing: US investment-grade corporate bond sales are expected t...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US corporate debt issuance is skyrocketing:
US investment-grade corporate bond sales are expected to rise +$37 billion YoY in November, or +27%, to $175 billion, the highest for any November on record.
This would mark a +$76 billion, or +77%, increase from November 2024 level.
To put this into perspective, the 5-year average before 2025 was $104 billion.
By comparison, US investment-grade bond issuance stood at ~$100 billion in October.
As a result, US investment-grade bond sales have risen to a record $1.76 trillion YTD, already surpassing the full-year 2025 total of $1.75 trillion.
Meanwhile, over $300 billion in AI-related corporate bonds have been issued in global investment-grade markets so far in 2026, almost 3 times the total for all of 2025.
AI spending is fueling an unprecedented wave of corporate borrowing.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META has built a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese robotics company Fourier & is already devel...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META has built a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese robotics company Fourier & is already developing a 2nd version.
The robot, internally called Max, stands nearly 5 feet tall, weighs about 106 pounds, & was developed in just 3 months.
It runs on NVIDIA’s Jetson Thor chip, features expressive eyes and a mouth, and has five-fingered hands capable of picking up small objects.
Meta reportedly sees humanoid robots as a potential physical extension of its Muse AI agent, capable of handling everyday household tasks.
The next version, Max 2, is being designed with improved hands, additional sensors to navigate stairs, and a built-in projector.
Meta is also hiring robotics engineers in China to help scale development toward mass production.
For now, the company says the prototypes are strictly for internal research, with no consumer launch timeline announced.
Source: The Information

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: It has been an exceptionally volatile earnings season: Information Technology stocks fell -1.2% on...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
It has been an exceptionally volatile earnings season:
Information Technology stocks fell -1.2% on average in October on the first trading day after reporting earnings, the weakest performance among all sectors.
This was followed by Energy and Consumer Staples, with average 1-day returns of -0.3% and -0.2%, respectively.
On the other hand, 8 out of 11 sectors recorded positive 1-day performance after reporting earnings over the same period.
Consumer Discretionary benefited the most, at +1.9%, followed by Healthcare and Industrials at +1.5% and +1.2%, respectively.
As a result, the average stock gained +0.6% on the first trading day after reporting earnings.
Tech is deviating from the rest of the market.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Americans have never been this pessimistic about their finances: A record 41% of US consumers expec...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Americans have never been this pessimistic about their finances:
A record 41% of US consumers expect their financial situation to be worse over the next 12 months.
This figure has more than tripled since Q2 2024.
By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, this metric peaked at 23%.
This proportion is also significantly higher than in the 1970s and the 1980s, when CPI inflation was above 10%.
Furthermore, 31% of US consumers believe their personal financial situation will be worse in 5 years, double the proportion seen in the 1980s.
Americans feel as though we are in a recession.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Short interest in the Nasdaq 100 ETF, $QQQ, is up to ~82 million shares, its highest since March 2023.
Over the last several weeks, this figure has surged +18 million shares, or +28%.
Year-to-date, short interest in $QQQ has nearly doubled.
Meanwhile, short interest in the S&P 500 ETF, $SPY, has declined -30 million shares since March, to ~92 million shares, near its lowest in at least 5 years.
By comparison, during the 2022 bear market, short interest peaked at ~90 million shares for $QQQ and ~180 million shares for $SPY.
Short interest in tech is very high right now.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: On days like today, it's important to zoom out. No, the AI Revolution is not "over," and the market...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
On days like today, it's important to zoom out.
No, the AI Revolution is not "over," and the market is not "going to zero."
In fact, the Nasdaq 100 is up +11% YTD and nearly +70% since its April 2025 low.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 is currently set to post a blended earnings +30.2% growth rate for Q3 2026.
This puts us on track for the third-straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
And, even after the biggest hack in crypto history, Bitcoin is down less than -5% this week.
Disruptive technologies like AI will inevitably bring heightened volatility, polarized positioning, and extreme swings in market sentiment.
However, do not let short-term volatility overshadow the broader picture.
We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in history.
Technical corrections are healthy, necessary, and an inevitable part of every bull market.
Do not lose sight of the bigger picture.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$TSLA EXPECTED TO OPEN OPTIMUS ROBOT RESERVATIONS IN EARLY DECEMBER: REPORT
Tesla is reportedly preparing to open consumer reservations for its Optimus humanoid robot in early December, potentially around the December 1-2 Humanoids Summit, according to The San Francisco Standard.
Tesla is also expected to demonstrate Optimus V3 at the event, with most initial units intended for businesses and a smaller number reserved for consumers.
The robot is expected to cost more than $20,000, although reservation deposits and final pricing remain unclear.
Tesla has already begun early production at its Fremont factory, but Musk recently said deliveries to outside customers aren't expected until late 2027, as the company continues working through AI, hardware and reliability challenges.
Tesla has not officially confirmed the reservation plans.

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC IN TALKS TO LEASE MAJOR AI DATA CENTER CAMPUS IN 🇨🇦 CANADA: GLOBE & MAIL Anthropic is r...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC IN TALKS TO LEASE MAJOR AI DATA CENTER CAMPUS IN 🇨🇦 CANADA: GLOBE & MAIL
Anthropic is reportedly negotiating with Beacon Data Centers to lease a large AI data center campus near Edmonton, Alberta.
The proposed site would feature four data halls powered by a 920 MW natural gas plant, which received regulatory approval on October 23.
Construction of the power plant is expected to begin in Q4 2026, with operations targeted for Q4 2027.
The potential deal comes just two weeks after Anthropic signed a 20-year lease for a separate 420 MW data center project in Nova Scotia.
The Alberta project would have roughly twice the power capacity of the Nova Scotia campus, adding to Anthropic's growing infrastructure commitments ahead of its planned IPO.
Talks remain ongoing, and no agreement has been announced.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The timing of today's market crash is noteworthy. As selling pressure spreads, the Nasdaq 100 is no...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The timing of today's market crash is noteworthy.
As selling pressure spreads, the Nasdaq 100 is now down nearly -5% on the day.
Meanwhile, the market-implied odds of a Democrat "sweep" in the Midterms next week has surged from 65% to 72% today, a record high.
That's +7 percentage points in 2 days amid this market downturn.
We have yet to receive a comment from the Trump Administration regarding the current situation in the market.
However, what is clear is that the timing of today's market crash will be consequential.
And, even as technology stocks drop sharply, US Treasury Yields are barely seeing any relief.
This leaves us with high rates, a falling stock market, $100+ oil prices, and rising CPI, PPI, and PCE inflation.
Next week is going to be interesting, to say the least.

You can now have all your AI agents working together in a virtual office.

item.title: @wallstengine: KALSHI RAISES $1B AT A $40 BILLION VALUATION Kalshi has closed a Series G co-led by Sequoia Capital...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
KALSHI RAISES $1B AT A $40 BILLION VALUATION
Kalshi has closed a Series G co-led by Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management.
Its valuation has climbed from $1B in June 2025 to $40B in just sixteen months.
Kalshi launched in 2021 after spending nearly four years securing federal regulation. It gained traction during the 2024 election, then reached a much wider audience after introducing sports contracts in early 2025.
Growth is now increasingly driven by markets beyond sports, including crypto, commodities, and new derivatives products:
"Kalshi continues to experience significant growth, with Q4 revenue currently on track to surpass Robinhood's revenue."
The new capital will support new products for retail and institutional customers, and international expansion.
Other investors include Morgan Stanley Investment Management, Baillie Gifford, Coatue and Andreessen Horowitz.
An IPO has also been discussed, though Tarek Mansour has not confirmed plans or provided a timeline.

item.title: @wallstengine: Ford $F CEO Jim Farley is targeting 5 million annual vehicle sales by 2032, roughly 20% above curre...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Ford $F CEO Jim Farley is targeting 5 million annual vehicle sales by 2032, roughly 20% above current levels.
Ford hasn't reached that volume since 2019, and its global vehicle deliveries are down 9% so far this year.
The company plans to introduce five new models priced below $40,000 by the end of the decade, including its $30,000 Fathom electric pickup, which is expected to begin production in Q4 2027.
Ford is targeting more than 100,000 Fathom sales in its first year, while also expanding its lineup in Europe through partnerships with Renault and Geely.
Source: WSJ

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC EXPECTED TO RECEIVE A “HIGH” JUNK CREDIT RATING AFTER IPO: FT Blackstone has told investo...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC EXPECTED TO RECEIVE A “HIGH” JUNK CREDIT RATING AFTER IPO: FT
Blackstone has told investors Anthropic is likely to receive a credit rating in the double-B range after going public, below investment grade, reversing its earlier expectations for an investment-grade rating by year-end.
The lower rating could make it more expensive for Anthropic to finance its massive AI infrastructure expansion, while limiting access to pension funds and insurers that face restrictions on investing in junk-rated debt.
The warning comes as Blackstone participates in Anthropic's $63B financing deal, known as Project North Star, to support the leasing of 1.5 GW of Google's AI chips.
Under the deal:
• More than $42B in senior loans are guaranteed by Broadcom $AVGO.
• Another $18B in junior debt is backed by Anthropic's lease payments.
• Blackstone's funds invested $9B in junior debt, earning yields above 10%.
Anthropic's IPO prospectus outlined plans to spend more than $800B on computing infrastructure through 2045.
Without an investment-grade rating, Anthropic may need to continue relying on financially stronger partners to support its borrowing.
The major credit agencies, Moody's, S&P and Fitch, have not yet formally issued ratings for Anthropic, per FT.

item.title: @wallstengine: Global Payments $GPN is being targeted in a potential $40B+ buyout by private equity firm Clayton,...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Global Payments $GPN is being targeted in a potential $40B+ buyout by private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, which has teamed up with GTCR, the company's largest shareholder, FT reports.
The payments processor has a market value of roughly $23B and more than $17B in net debt. A deal including a takeover premium would rank among the largest leveraged buyouts in history.
Interestingly, GTCR became Global Payments' largest outside shareholder through its 2025 Worldpay acquisition, a deal that drew investor criticism over increased debt and dilution.
Global Payments shares subsequently fell to near-decade lows, attracting activist investor Elliott Management.
Talks are ongoing, and no agreement has been reached.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Subvocal has raised $1.3M for smart glasses that turn silently mouthed words into text, in a pre-seed round led by Afore Capital with participation from Y Combinator and angel investors.
The glasses use radar to detect tiny movements in your speech muscles. The company says its AI converts those movements into text at more than 200 words per minute.
Think writing an email, replying in Slack or prompting an AI without touching a keyboard or reading your message aloud to everyone around you.
It only decodes words you deliberately mouth, not your thoughts.

item.title: @wallstengine: Starbucks $SBUX CEO Brian Niccol says the company could eventually expand beyond coffee and become...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Starbucks $SBUX CEO Brian Niccol says the company could eventually expand beyond coffee and become a multi-brand business, similar to Yum Brands, which owns Taco Bell and KFC.
“Our scale provides an opportunity to go beyond just being a one-brand company.”
“You put other businesses into a portfolio that can leverage the strength of Starbucks — that could be an interesting proposition, down the road.”
Niccol added that he would “never say never” to acquisitions, although Starbucks remains focused on its own turnaround and doesn't need deals to meet its growth targets.
The comments come weeks after Starbucks dismissed rumors of a potential Chipotle takeover.
